(a) The Space gesture is ONE state machine spanning `onKeyDown` (C19ae, out of scope, cited by name only — sets `state.spaceDown=true`/`state._spaceAt=now` on Space keydown when no field has focus and Cmd/Ctrl is not held, per the issue's own citation of C19ae 9992-10000) and `onKeyUp` (this scope, 10221-10234). `onKeyUp` reads `wasDown=state.spaceDown` (10225), computes `held` from `state._spaceAt` (10226, `performance.now()` with a `Date.now()` fallback), and derives `tapped=wasDown&&!state.spaceUsedForPan&&held<SPACE_TAP_MS` (10227, threshold 250ms, 10220) — a tap only counts if the hold was never used to pan. It then unconditionally resets `state.spaceDown`/`state.isPanning`/`state.spaceUsedForPan` to `false` (10228), restores the tool cursor from a per-tool map (10229), and finally calls `togglePlay()` (10233) if `tapped` AND the tool is not `'pen'` with an in-progress `_pen.path` (the one place, per the 10230-10232 comment, the tap gesture is suppressed so a half-drawn Pen path isn't stranded). A separate `else if(event.key==='Alt')` branch (10234) clears `state.altDown` on Alt release, unconditionally, no tap/hold distinction. `window.addEventListener('blur',…)` (10241-10243) is a second-layer safety net: it force-resets `state.spaceDown`/`state.isPanning`/`state.spaceUsedForPan`/`state.altDown` on window blur, per the 10235-10240 comment, to cover any OS shortcut (Spotlight named explicitly) that steals focus before the keyup itself reaches the page. The capture-phase `document.addEventListener('pointerdown',…,true)` at 10249 sets `state.spaceUsedForPan=true` whenever `state.spaceDown` is already true at pointerdown time — per its own 10244-10248 comment, this is a SEPARATE mechanism from either pan implementation (`tools.js` Paper.js path, `viewtools-bridge.js` Rust-engine path, both out of scope) specifically because panning is implemented twice and a single capture-phase flag avoids having to touch both.

(b) Line 10251 (`document.addEventListener('keydown',onKeyDown);document.addEventListener('keyup',onKeyUp);`) is confirmed by a whole-file grep to be the ONLY place `onKeyDown` or `onKeyUp` is passed to `addEventListener` for the page-level `keydown`/`keyup` events — every other `addEventListener('keydown'/'keyup',…)` call in timeline.js (lines 5443, 5708, 5939, 7664, 7721, 8246, 8349, 8568, 8917, 10279, 10298, 10488, 10957, 11059) registers its own distinct inline/named handler, none of them `onKeyDown`/`onKeyUp`. This single registration is the extraction seed for the whole keyboard subsystem: cutting it would silently disable both the shortcut table (C19ae) and the entire Space tap/hold machine (packet 1) in one line.

(c) The Cmd-hold machine (packet 2, 2026-08-27, feedback #64): `_cmdHoldEligible()` (10274-10278) returns false whenever focus is on an INPUT/SELECT/TEXTAREA/contentEditable element, OR `state.playing`, OR `state.tool` is already `'select'`/`'subselect'`, OR the Pen tool has an in-progress path (`_pen&&_pen.path`, `_pen` module-scoped in tools.js:7128), OR `state.spaceDown` is true. The `keydown` listener (10279-10297) only acts on `e.key==='Meta'||e.key==='Control'`: it guards against native modifier auto-repeat via `_cmdHoldDown` (10281), then arms a `setTimeout(…,CMD_HOLD_MS)` (180ms, 10273) ONLY if `_cmdHoldEligible()` passes at press time (10283); the timer body re-checks both `_cmdHoldDown` and `_cmdHoldEligible()` (10286, in case state changed during the wait) before recording `_cmdHoldPrevTool=state.tool` (10287) and calling `window.SM.setTool('select')` (10288). Any OTHER keydown while `_cmdHoldTimer` is pending (10290-10296) clears the timer silently — per the 10291-10294 comment, this is what lets the ~15 existing Cmd+<letter> shortcuts in `onKeyDown` (whose own Cmd/Ctrl+key handlers are gated on `event.metaKey`/`event.ctrlKey`, out of scope) fire normally: the modifier's own keydown fires first and would otherwise flicker the tool before the letter's keydown lands, which the 10259-10264 lead-in comment names explicitly as the hazard this arm-delay avoids. The `keyup` listener (10298-10303) restores `_cmdHoldPrevTool` via `window.SM.setTool(...)` if one was recorded, or simply clears the pending timer if the hold never actually armed. `window.addEventListener('blur',…)` (10307-10311) is the same stuck-modifier safety net shape as packet 1's own blur handler, restoring `_cmdHoldPrevTool` if focus is lost mid-hold. Line 10312 (`document.querySelectorAll('.tool-btn').forEach(…SM.setTool(this.dataset.tool)…)`) is the generic, ALL-tool-buttons click handler; by direct read it does NOT itself reference any `_cmdHold*` variable and does not explicitly cancel the hold — the issue's own suggested table describes it as ".tool-btn click cancelling the hold", which this census records as an over-statement of the code's own behavior (see `future_proposals`); it is included in packet 2's range because it is the line immediately preceding packet 3's own lead-in and shares no clearer boundary.

(d) The shape-tool flyout (packet 3, 2026-08, feedback quoted in the 10313-10314 lead-in): `SHAPE_TOOLS=['rect','line','ellipse','speechbubble','star']` (10328); `LPRESS_MS=450` (10329, long-press threshold). `ensureFront(tool)` (10330-10336) is a no-op for a non-shape tool (10331) and otherwise toggles the `.stack-front` class on exactly one `.tool-btn[data-tool=…]` per call, front-ing the picked tool's own button in the shared stack. `window.SMShapeGroup={ensureFront:ensureFront}` (10337) is the sole external-facing surface, read by `setTool` (timeline.js:435) and `tutorial.js` (tutorial.js:1468) — confirmed the two ONLY readers by a whole-`src` grep, matching the 10322-10326 lead-in exactly. `closeFlyout`/`onOutsideDown` (10338-10339) are one-line helpers: the former removes the flyout element and its own outside-click listener, the latter closes on any pointerdown outside the flyout element. `openFlyout(originBtn)` (10340-10360) builds a fresh `<div class="shape-tool-flyout">` positioned relative to `originBtn`'s own `getBoundingClientRect()` (clamped to the viewport via `Math.min`/`Math.max` against `window.innerWidth`/`window.innerHeight`, 10357-10358), with one button per `SHAPE_TOOLS` entry cloning the real button's own `innerHTML` (stripping any `<span class="sk">` shortcut-key badge, 10350) whose click both fronts the tool (`ensureFront(t)`) and switches to it (`window.SM.setTool(t)`, 10352) before closing the flyout. The long-press vs. click distinction lives entirely in the `#shape-tool-stack` element's own three listeners (10361-10371): `pointerdown` arms a `setTimeout(…,LPRESS_MS)` that sets `suppressClick=true` and opens the flyout (10366-10367); `pointerup`/`pointerleave` both clear the pending timer (10369, short press never opens the flyout); a CAPTURE-phase `click` listener on the stack itself (10370) calls `ev.stopImmediatePropagation()` when `suppressClick` is true, preventing the long-press's own trailing click from ALSO reaching the bubble-phase `.tool-btn` click handler (packet 2's own line 10312) that would otherwise fire `SM.setTool` a second time for the ORIGINAL (un-fronted) button.

(e) The four colour-field pairs (packet 4) all read `this.dataset.hex8||this.value` (10383, 10384, 10391, 10392), the CLAUDE.md §2 alpha-colour convention, on every `input` event — confirmed to never read `.value` alone. `#color-fill`/`#color-stroke` (the native `<input type="color">` wells) and `#pm-fill-c`/`#pm-stroke-c` (the mini popover swatches) additionally call `window.SM.setFillEnabled(true)`/`setStrokeEnabled(true)` (10383-10384, 10391-10392) whenever fill/stroke was OFF, per the 10374-10382 comment ("Actively picking a fill color also ENABLES fill", Graphite-style, deliberately keyed to genuine user `input` events only — programmatic `.value` writes on load/selection-sync don't dispatch `input` and so can't silently re-enable). `#pm-fill-c`/`#pm-stroke-c` (10384, 10392) additionally call `setHex8Input(document.getElementById('color-fill'/'color-stroke'), v)` (app.js:560) to mirror the popover's own picked value back into the toolbar's native colour well, keeping both colour surfaces in sync; `#color-fill`/`#color-stroke` themselves do not call `setHex8Input` (their own downstream sync, if any, is inside `SM.setFillColor`/`setStrokeColor`'s own bodies, timeline.js:608/615, out of scope). `#p-fill-on` (10385) and the `-lp` eye-badge clicks (10389-10390) are PURE toggles — `setFillEnabled(this.checked)` / `setFillEnabled(!state.fillEnabled)` / `setStrokeEnabled(!state.strokeEnabled)` — with no colour read at all. The 10386-10388 comment states that the OLD `fill-enable-toggle`/`stroke-enable-toggle` section-header buttons were removed per redesign and that 'every other reference to those old IDs is null-guarded'; by direct grep of src/index.html at the frozen SHA, `#fill-enable-toggle-lp` (index.html:257) and `#stroke-enable-toggle-lp` (index.html:253) BOTH EXIST as `.cw-eye` divs — present, not absent — so lines 10389-10390 resolve to real elements and are not the null-guarded references the comment describes (those, if any, are elsewhere in the codebase, out of scope); neither line itself contains a null guard on the `getElementById` result.

(f) Every `state.*` field this scope reads or writes, with line: `state.spaceDown` (read 10225/10228→written-false/10242→written-false/10249/10277; written-true only in C19ae's `onKeyDown`, out of scope), `state._spaceAt` (read 10226, written only in C19ae, out of scope), `state.spaceUsedForPan` (read 10227/10249→written-true; written-false 10228/10242), `state.isPanning` (written-false 10228/10242), `state.tool` (read 10229/10233/10276/10287/10349), `state.altDown` (written-false 10234/10242), `state.playing` (read 10276), `state.fillEnabled` (read 10383/10384/10389), `state.strokeEnabled` (read 10390/10391/10392). No `state.*` field is written by packets 3 or 4 beyond what `window.SM.*` setters perform internally (out of scope). Every `window.SM.*` method this scope calls, with owner line (definitions in the `window.SM={…}` block, timeline.js:349+): `setTool` (defined 373; called 10288, 10302, 10310, 10312, 10352), `setBrushSize` (defined 520; called 10373), `setFillColor` (defined 615; called 10383, 10384), `setFillEnabled` (defined 647; called 10383, 10384, 10385, 10389), `setStrokeColor` (defined 608; called 10391, 10392), `setStrokeEnabled` (defined 654; called 10390, 10391, 10392).

(g) Every DOM id/class this scope touches (src/index.html consumer): ids `p-sw`, `color-fill`, `pm-fill-c`, `p-fill-on`, `fill-enable-toggle-lp`, `stroke-enable-toggle-lp`, `color-stroke`, `pm-stroke-c`, `shape-tool-stack` (all confirmed present by grep, see `reconciliation`); classes/selectors `.tool-btn`, `.tool-btn[data-tool="…"]`, `.stack-front` (toggled, not confirmed present as a CSS rule — out of scope, style.css), `.shape-tool-flyout`/`.shape-tool-flyout-item`/`.active` (created dynamically by `openFlyout`, not present in static markup).

(h) Callers: everything in this scope is self-registering top-level code (module-load-time `addEventListener` calls, an immediately-invoked function expression, and direct `getElementById(…).addEventListener(…)` chains) — none of the eleven named functions/handlers this scope defines (`onKeyUp`, the anonymous `blur`/`pointerdown`/`keydown`/`keyup` handlers, `_cmdHoldEligible`, `ensureFront`, `closeFlyout`, `onOutsideDown`, `openFlyout`, and the anonymous field-change/input handlers) has an external caller, EXCEPT `window.SMShapeGroup.ensureFront`, read by `setTool` (timeline.js:435) and `tutorial.js` (tutorial.js:1468) — confirmed the only two readers by a whole-`src` grep. Adds a window-blur safety net and a capture-phase pointerdown flag-setter for the pan gesture. Ends with the ONE page-level registration of both `onKeyDown` and `onKeyUp`, the extraction seed for the whole keyboard subsystem (boundary (b)).

future_proposals: The issue's own suggested packet-2 description labels line 10312 (`.tool-btn` click → `SM.setTool`) as "cancelling the hold"; by direct read the line does not reference any `_cmdHold*` variable and performs no cancellation of its own — a mouse click on a tool button while the Cmd-hold arm-timer is pending would switch tools via this line WITHOUT clearing `_cmdHoldTimer`, so if the timer later fires it re-checks `_cmdHoldEligible()` (which fails once `state.tool` is `'select'`/`'subselect'`, but would still pass and force a switch back to `'select'` if the user clicked, say, `'draw'`→still-not-select). Not confirmed as a user-visible defect by execution; flagged for awareness since the issue's own prose describes a causal link the code does not literally implement.

The 10386-10388 comment asserts old removed-ID references are all null-guarded, but lines 10389-10390 (`#fill-enable-toggle-lp`/`#stroke-enable-toggle-lp`) themselves chain `getElementById(...).addEventListener(...)` with NO null guard — currently safe only because both ids are confirmed present in src/index.html (boundaries (e)); a future markup change removing either id without also removing/guarding these two lines would throw at script-load time (`Cannot read properties of null`), taking down the rest of timeline.js's own top-level init code that follows. Not confirmed as a current defect; flagged for awareness given the comment's own (currently inaccurate) claim of blanket null-guarding.

`openFlyout` (10340-10360) clamps its own position against `window.innerWidth`/`window.innerHeight` but never re-clamps on window resize while the flyout is open — a flyout opened near the right/bottom edge and then followed by a window resize could render partially off-screen. Not confirmed as a reported defect by execution; noted for awareness, not flagged as a required fix.
